title: GridForge Spreadsheet - Harbor Run QC
subtitle: OpenHands gpt-5.6-sol xhigh model run scored 0.8413 on 2026-08-22.
note: Scope: run-backed analysis of jobs/gridforge-gpt-5.6-sol-xhigh-02. The bundled run_inventory.py did not recognize this Harbor trial naming shape, so evidence is taken from result.json, verifier/report.json, verifier/test-stdout.txt, and generated app artifacts.

runs.note: Valid graded run: no_op=0, graded=1. Failed 3 of 21 browser criteria.

tasks.name: GridForge
tasks.headline: The model run is valid and still too high: three strong verifiers failed, but 18/21 passed, so the task needs additional strict coverage to push model score below 0.7.

findings.what: The model failed the formula reference-click edge case. The verifier reported that insertRef() drops the leading '=' when formula editor content is fully selected.
findings.why: The generated insertRef() uses the editor selection and replaces the selected text with a raw reference, so a fully selected '=' can become 'B2' instead of '=B2'.
findings.impact: This is a real model miss and a useful breaker, but it only costs 1.5 weight, so it is not enough to lower the model below target by itself.
findings.fix: Keep this verifier and add adjacent formula-authoring checks around selection replacement, editing mid-formula, dragging references after typed operators, and preserving '=' through all reference-pick paths.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by verifier report: formula_bar_raw_formula_and_precedence value=0.0, weight=1.5, reasoning says insertRef() drops the leading '=' and breaks the required raw-formula workflow.

findings.what: The model failed the single Replace exact-value check: replacing target in C20='target-B' produced C20='FOUND-B' instead of exactly 'FOUND'.
findings.why: The generated replaceOne() performs substring replacement with raw(a).replace(regex(), replacement). The verifier intentionally checks selected-match replacement semantics, not just substring substitution.
findings.impact: This is a clean confirmed failure and shows the verifier is catching spreadsheet behavior beyond simple text replacement, but it costs only 1.5 weight.
findings.fix: Keep this check and consider splitting find navigation, replace-current-cell exactness, and replace-all atomic undo into separate criteria so partial implementations lose more score.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by verifier report: find_replace_navigation_atomic value=0.0, weight=1.5; Find Next and Replace All passed, but single Replace produced C20='FOUND-B'.

findings.what: The model accepted a forged save where Riley's live sessionId was paired with userId='morgan', returning HTTP 200 and attributing the revision to Morgan.
findings.why: The generated save route validates that body.userId exists, but does not verify that body.sessionId belongs to that same user. The presence endpoint checks session ownership more strictly than save.
findings.impact: This is a high-value confirmed failure because it proves the server trust-boundary verifier can catch impersonation that UI-only tests miss.
findings.fix: Keep this verifier at high weight, and add one more direct API trust-boundary criterion for workbook/sheet metadata immutability or revision-list immutation after rejected probes.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by verifier report: forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections value=0.0, weight=2.0; the mismatched valid userId probe returned HTTP 200, advanced revision to 87, and attributed the write to 'morgan'.

findings.what: The current model score is 0.8413, above the target of <0.7, because only 5.0 of 31.5 total weight failed.
findings.why: The task has good hard checks, but the model passed many medium/high-weight criteria including range functions, circular recovery, fill formulas, revision restore, stale conflicts, and live presence.
findings.impact: If shipped as-is, the task may not break the target model strongly enough even though several individual verifiers are good.
findings.fix: Tighten or split existing passed complex areas rather than adding vague new requirements: formula editing edge cases, range operations, live collaboration, and API trust-boundary checks are the best places to harvest additional failures.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by Harbor result: browser_passed=18, browser_total=21, browser_score=0.8413; failed weights are 1.5 + 1.5 + 2.0 = 5.0.

blocks.title: Tightening Direction
items: Split partial-pass compound checks where the model already failed one sub-path.
Add stricter formula authoring edge cases around selected text, reference replacement, and caret preservation.
Add more direct API trust-boundary probes because the model already missed one server-side identity invariant.
